name: Warm Graphite Light Lab
origin: Our own look, from Colour_v1 (Sam's pick, 21 Nov 2026)
head: Fraunces
label: JetBrains Mono

rules.Texture and light: Film grain 4.5%, faint red, green and blue corner glows; colours add like real light
rules.Motion: One slow move per shot (3% or less), entrances 0.6-0.9 s, no overshoot
rules.Transition: Push-through from the last shot's key picture (0.6 s)
rules.Best for: Light, colour and vision; documentaries built on real documents

rules.Texture and light: Matte grain 12%, soft vignette 32%, faint hairline grid
rules.Motion: Calm version: one slow move per shot, staggered reveals
rules.Transition: Hard cut that keeps the focal point within 25% of the screen
rules.Best for: Archive-led stories: old papers, photos, maps

name: Void
origin: Studied: LEMMiNO, 'The Universal S' (measured: 53% of pixels near-black #181818)
take: Huge black negative space; one small object or line of type at a time; wide-tracked caps
change: Warmer crimson accent and our serif for spoken lines; no imitation of LEMMiNO's titles or logo
head: IBM Plex Sans Condensed
label: IBM Plex Mono

rules.Texture and light: Almost none: 3% grain, deep vignette, objects lit as if under one lamp
rules.Motion: Very slow push-ins, long holds of 4-6 s on one object
rules.Transition: Cut to black for a beat, then the next object
rules.Best for: Mysteries and cold opens: the eye in the dark, the shuttered room

name: Map Room
origin: Studied: Johnny Harris, 'How Europe Stole Africa so Quickly, Mapped' (teal room, parchment maps, sepia)
take: Parchment maps and documents on a dark teal ground; hand-marked annotations
change: No host on camera; our maps are drawn, not printed and filmed; brass instead of marker yellow
head: Libre Caslon Text
label: Courier Prime

rules.Texture and light: Paper grain and fibre on every card; a soft desk-lamp falloff
rules.Motion: Slow pans across a map; routes draw on; pins drop and settle
rules.Transition: Zoom from one place on the map into the next document
rules.Best for: Places and journeys: the lapis route (ep 5), Manchester and Kendal (ep 1)

name: Federal Print
origin: Studied: Phil Edwards, 'How the US government got hip graphic design' (black ground, white paper scans, red and steel blue)
take: Real printed pages on black; bold modernist type; red and steel-blue labels
change: No host on camera; our own grid and labels; film-strip framing used sparingly
head: Inter Tight
label: IBM Plex Mono

rules.Texture and light: Light halftone on scans; crisp edges; no glows
rules.Motion: Pages slide in on a grid; labels stamp on; one bold word fills the frame
rules.Transition: Hard cut on the beat; film-strip wipe between chapters
rules.Best for: Design and print history; pigment and dye stories (ep 5)
